Hon'ble Alok Mahra, J.
Mr. Lalit Sharma, learned counsel for the applicant.
2. Mr. Deepak Bisht, learned DAG for the State.
3. Ms. Suraiya Naaz, learned counsel for respondent no.2.

4. Present C482 application is filed with the prayer to quash judgment and order dated 15.01.2024 passed by the Addl. Session Judge, Vikasnagar, Dehradun in Criminal Revision No.37 of 2023 and order dated 04.07.2023 passed by the Addl. Chief Judicial Magistrate, Vikasnagar, Dehradun in Criminal Case No.342 of 2019, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 120B and 427 of IPC on the basis of compromise between the parties.

entities.text: Addl. Chief Judicial Magistrate, Vikasnagar, Dehradun
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 5. Compounding application (IA/3/2024) is also filed in the matter wherein it is prayed to compound the offence between the parties under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 120B and 427 of IPC.
6. Parties are present before this Court today and duly identified by their respective counsels.
Parties have also filed their respective affidavits stating the above fact of compromise between them.
7. Learned State Counsel has formally opposed the compounding application.

8. Hon'ble Supreme Court, in a catena of its judgments, has observed that in cases where because of the compromise arrived at between the parties possibility of conviction is remote and bleak, the High Court may quash the criminal proceedings as continuation of the same would cause great prejudice and injustice to the accused.
9. In view of the above, Compounding Application is allowed.

As a result, the judgment and order dated 15.01.2024 passed by the Addl. Session Judge, Vikasnagar, Dehradun in Criminal Revision No.37 of 2023 and order dated 04.07.2023 passed by the Addl. Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Vikasnagar, Dehradun in Criminal Case No.342 of 2019, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 120B and 427 of IPC are hereby quashed qua the applicant.
